case_title: Jaikam Khan v. The State of Uttar Pradesh
accused_victim_relationship: Relative: Momin Khan was a son of the deceased father and brother of the deceased Shaukeen Khan; Jaikam Khan was a first cousin; Sajid was a nephew of Momin Khan. Prior dispute over management of a brick-kiln and its accounts involving Momin Khan and the family.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 r/w s.34; Arms Act s.25/4
weapon: Knives (knife, chhuriyan and a daav recovered by the police)
evidence_type: Eyewitness testimony of two interested, related witnesses; recovery of weapons and clothes; arrest evidence; site plans; FIR; forensic and fingerprint material (not relied on)
confession: Alleged confession by the accused recorded in the arrest-cum-recovery memo (Ex Ka-49); not relied on beyond facts distinctly discovered under s.27 Evidence Act
aggravating_circumstances: Six persons killed with knives, including a woman, a child aged about 8 and elderly parents
trial_court_outcome: All four accused convicted under IPC s.302/34 and sentenced to death; accused 1, 3 and 4 also convicted under Arms Act s.25/4 with three years RI and fine of Rs 5,000
high_court_outcome: Appeals of accused 1, 3 and 4 dismissed and death sentence confirmed; accused 2 (Nazra) acquitted
neutral_facts: On the evening of 23 January 2014, around 8.30 pm, six members of one family were attacked and killed with knives at their house in a village. The prosecution case is that four persons, including the accused, entered the family compound carrying knives. According to the prosecution, the victims were killed in the courtyard, the verandah, rooms in the middle portion of the house and an upstairs room. Two relatives of the victims who were present in the house said they hid and watched the attack; their accounts formed the main eyewitness evidence. Villagers gathered after the incident. The surviving relatives went to the police station to lodge a written report and a first information report was registered. The investigating officer prepared site plans on the basis of information given by the witnesses. Later that night police arrested three of the accused at a crossroads and recovered knives from a room and from open fields near the house, following statements attributed to the accused. Blood-stained clothes were later recovered from another house. Forensic science reports were obtained. A fingerprint expert report and a dog squad report were not placed on record, and no independent villager witness was examined.
physical_harm: Six persons killed by knife assaults; injuries not described in detail in the judgment
premeditation_planning: Not found by the Supreme Court; the trial court's finding of a pre-planned crime was held to be conjecture
motive: alleged: dispute over management and accounts of a brick-kiln between Momin Khan and the deceased father, brother and PW-1. Court held no motive proved against accused 3 and 4 and no strong motive proved against accused 1
key_evidence_accepted: Court accepted only that the two eyewitnesses could at most have seen the assault on some of the deceased; it did not accept the eyewitness account as sufficient alone, and rejected the clothes recovery and the s.27 recoveries
witness_credibility: PW-1 and PW-2 are interested and related witnesses, neither wholly reliable nor wholly unreliable; their version is hard to reconcile with the site plans and they could not have seen all assaults. Investigating officer admitted their hideouts were not recorded in the site plan
post_offence_conduct: Prosecution alleged the accused fled through the rear gate, returned and changed clothes; the court found this a mystery and gave no weight to it
trial_duration: offence: 23 January 2014; trial judgment: 2 January 2016; High Court: 18 May 2018; Supreme Court: 15 December 2021
legal_representation: Accused 1: Smt. Nitya Ramakrishnan, Senior Counsel; Accused 3 and 4: Shri Dama Seshadri Naidu; PW-1 (appellant against acquittal of accused 2): Shri Anant Agarwal; State of Uttar Pradesh: Shri Vinod Diwakar, AAG
investigation_status: FIR registered on PW-1's complaint; investigation completed; charge-sheet filed; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: No independent villager witnesses examined; fingerprint expert report and dog squad report not placed on record; the trial court's reasoning was criticised as conjectural
appeal_history: Trial court: all four convicted under s.302/34 IPC and sentenced to death. High Court: accused 1, 3, 4 appeals dismissed and death sentence confirmed; accused 2 acquitted. Supreme Court: appeals of accused 1, 3, 4 allowed; PW-1's appeal against acquittal of accused 2 dismissed
prosecution_argument: Concurrent findings of conviction should not be disturbed; absence of kitchen and bathroom in site plans is not fatal; eyewitness testimony corroborated by the FIR; discrepancies not fatal to ocular evidence; accused gave no explanation under s.313
defence_argument: Eyewitnesses are interested and related; site plans omit kitchen and bathroom; independent witnesses not examined; no call made on mobile phones and C.D.Rs rejected; recoveries of clothes and weapons farcical; no motive for accused 3 and 4; no reasons for death sentence
legal_principle_applied: Interested witnesses scrutinised with care and corroboration required where neither wholly reliable nor wholly unreliable; non-examination of independent witnesses leads to adverse inference; s.27 admits only information distinctly relating to discovery; motive relevant where eyewitnesses are not wholly reliable; prosecution must prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt
precedent_relied_upon: Vadivelu Thevar v. State of Madras (1957) SCR 981; State of Rajasthan v. Teja Singh (2001) 3 SCC 147; Joydeb Patra v. State of West Bengal (2014) 12 SCC 444; State of Punjab v. Jagir Singh (1974) 3 SCC 277; Anand Ramachandra Chougule v. Sidarai Laxman Chougala (2019) 8 SCC 50; Piara Singh v. State of Punjab (1977) 4 SCC 452 and Anil Phukan v. State of Assam (1993) 3 SCC 282 (referred); Pulukuri Kottayya v. King Emperor AIR 1947 PC 67 (referred)
other_sentence_order: Release of accused 1, 3 and 4 forthwith if not required in any other offence; PW-1's appeal against acquittal of accused 2 dismissed; court deprecated the manner in which the trial court and High Court dealt with the death sentence

victim_gender.quote: Deceased Shanno (aged about 30 years) is the wife of deceased Shaukeen Khan, whereas deceased Samad (aged about 8 years) is the son of deceased Shaukeen Khan

accused_victim_relationship.quote: Appellant-Jaikam Khan (A-3) is the first cousin of deceased Shaukeen Khan, appellant-Momin Khan (A-1) and P.W.1-Ali Sher Khan.

statutory_provisions.quote: framed charges for the offences punishable under Section 302/34 of the IPC and under Section 25/4 of the Indian Arms Act, 1878

weapon.quote: All these accused persons were holding knife and chhuriyan (small knife) in their hands.

evidence_type.quote: the Court is satisfied that the evidence is creditworthy, then there is no bar on the court in relying on such evidence

confession.quote: All the statements made therein with regard to the confession of committing the crime would not be admissible in evidence.

aggravating_circumstances.quote: Even if the evidence of P.W.1-Ali Sher Khan and P.W.2-Jaan Mohammad is taken at its face value, the accused have murdered six deceased at different places.

trial_court_outcome.quote: convicted all the four accused for the offence punishable under Section 302/34 of the IPC and sentenced them to death

high_court_outcome.quote: dismissed the appeals of appellants- accused Nos. 1, 3 and 4 and confirmed the death sentence awarded to them

final_outcome.quote: Criminal Appeal Nos. 440-441 of 2020 filed by Momin Khan (Accused No.1); Criminal Appeal Nos. 434-436 of 2020 filed by Jaikam Khan (Accused No.3)... are allowed

offence_finally_established.quote: We, therefore, find that the prosecution has utterly failed to prove the case beyond reasonable doubt.

imprisonment_type.quote: are directed to be released forthwith, if not required in any other offence.

neutral_facts.quote: On hearing the cries of the deceased and others, many villagers gathered and all four accused fled from the spot through the back-door.

attempt_completion.quote: assaulted Mausam Khan (father), Asgari (mother), Shaukeen Khan (brother), Shanno (sister-in-law), Samad (nephew) and Muskan (niece) and killed them brutally

physical_harm.quote: assaulted Mausam Khan (father), Asgari (mother), Shaukeen Khan (brother), Shanno (sister-in-law), Samad (nephew) and Muskan (niece) and killed them brutally

number_of_offences.quote: framed charges for the offences punishable under Section 302/34 of the IPC and under Section 25/4 of the Indian Arms Act, 1878

premeditation_planning.quote: all the observations are nothing but conjectures and surmises, without there being any evidentiary support to them

motive.quote: with regard to Jaikam Khan (A-3) and Sajid (A-4), the prosecution has utterly failed to prove any motive

key_evidence_accepted.quote: They would fall in the category of 'neither wholly reliable nor wholly unreliable'

appeal_history.quote: dismissed the appeals of appellants- accused Nos. 1, 3 and 4 and confirmed the death sentence awarded to them
